title: Merovingian Empire
capsule: The final phase of Merovingian kingship in Francia, when the throne passed rapidly between the shadow-kings Dagobert III (711-715), Chilperic II (715-721) and the short-lived anti-king Chlothar IV (717-718), each a figurehead under whichever mayor of the palace held real power. This was an era of civil war among the Frankish nobility: after Pepin of Herstal's death in 714, the Neustrian mayor Ragenfrid, backed by Chilperic II and allied with the Frisians, contested control with the rising Austrasian strongman Charles Martel. Charles's victories over Ragenfrid's forces at Amblève (716) and Vincy (717) broke Neustrian resistance, even as a Merovingian king still nominally occupied the throne.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Core Frankish territories in Gaul and the Rhineland are well attested by royal diplomas, capitularies, and ecclesiastical records from the sixth century onward; the extent of tributary or nominal Frankish authority over peripheral peoples such as Bretons and Basques is less precisely bounded. Capsule researched for this polity/era specifically (confidence: high).
